note: Irregularities, conflicts between two official sources, and values that could not be confirmed. Each is published on the Flagged for review page with its source links and the manual step that would close it. Flags never block publication; they tell a reader what not to trust yet. Numbering is continuous across sessions, and a resolved flag is kept rather than deleted so the audit trail survives.

flags.title: Submitted tokens are 9 characters, not 10
flags.detail: All five submitted tokens (B04G1MEwY, B02NbDxp3, B00hJ57DV, B0c8moW59, B0f3GKalj) are 9 characters long. The observed amazon.com product identifiers in S04 are all 10 characters, and secondary sources describe ASINs as 10-character identifiers. No Amazon-owned definition was retrieved (see FLG-012). Because the intended ASIN cannot be confirmed, the intended ASIN, official listing URL, confirmation date and confirmation source are left blank for every row.
flags.manual_step: Confirm the intended product for each submitted link in Associates Central (or in the Amazon product page you intended) and supply the full 10-character ASIN or product URL.

flags.title: Observed destination ASIN differs from the token in the link
flags.detail: The short links resolved to different 10-character ASINs than the submitted token (for example B04G1MEwY resolved to B0CDY277D3). The observed destinations are recorded in separate fields and are not treated as the intended product. The site links to the observed destination only as a tagged, observed product (see FLG-005).
flags.manual_step: Open each submitted short link in a signed-in browser and confirm the product shown. Confirm whether the intended product is the observed product before it is published as the buy link.

flags.title: Compliance status of the supplied short links is unresolved
flags.detail: The short links are not claimed to be invalid. Associates Program Policies Participation Requirements (w) restrict a link-shortening service in a manner that makes it unclear that the link goes to an Amazon Site (S02). Whether the link.amazon short links fall within that restriction has not been determined. The site does not use the short links for outbound links; they appear only as source evidence. Added 2026-11-20: Amazon's Associates help (S13) states that Amazon full links and Amazon short links are supported in the OneLink setup, and that third-party shortened links are not. Participation Requirements 2(a) requires the Associates tag as a parameter in each Special Link (S02). None of the four observed product redirects contains a tag parameter (see products). Attribution of the link.amazon links to shopnow047c-20 therefore remains unconfirmed, and this flag stays open.
flags.manual_step: Check the supplied short links against Associates Program Policies (w) and the Associates tracking reports. Decide whether to keep them as evidence only or to replace them completely.

flags.title: One submitted link (B00hJ57DV) initially appeared not to resolve to a product
flags.detail: The link landed on an Amazon 'Continue shopping' checkpoint page with no product title, price or ASIN. The fetch was not a signed-in browser session, so the result may depend on session, region or timing. No product is shown for this row and no buy link is published. — RESOLVED 2026-11-20: this link does resolve; see resolution field.
flags.manual_step: Open the link in a signed-in browser. Supply the intended product URL if it can be identified.
flags.resolution: Superseded 2026-11-20: B00hJ57DV was re-fetched and resolved to B08DKYBTPH (Chefman 8 Qt TurboFry). The earlier "Continue shopping" checkpoint was an intermittent bot-check, not a dead link. Kept for the audit trail rather than deleted. Check it by hand: https://link.amazon/B00hJ57DV should land on https://www.amazon.com/dp/B08DKYBTPH

flags.title: Tagged Special Links are not yet validated in Associates Central
flags.detail: The product register contains draft /dp/ URLs with the Associates tracking ID, but they are not published as product links. They have not been generated or tested in Associates Central, and no tracking report has been reviewed because the sandbox has no Associates login. Gate G-02 requires a per-product test, destination confirmation, tracking-report reference, date and source before these links can render.
flags.manual_step: In Associates Central, generate one Special Link per intended product, click it, confirm its destination and tracking-report entry, then record each result in the product validation record. The publishing gate remains closed until all five records are complete.

flags.title: Associates account status and declared site are unknown
flags.detail: Associates help states that tags must be embedded in links on the sites declared in the application (S11). The declared site URL and account approval status are unknown to this build. The qualifying-sales requirement (three within 180 days) is also stated (S11).
flags.manual_step: Confirm that the Associates account declares the GitHub Pages URL (https://karagemop466-tech.github.io/Affil3/) or a custom domain for it, and that the account is active.

flags.title: Content depth is below the official 'robust content' rule of thumb
flags.detail: The Associates help text says a rule of thumb is at least 10 posts (S11). The site has 5 guides and 5 product rows. Adding content is a decision for the user (see suggestion S-07).
flags.manual_step: Decide the content plan (suggestion S-07) before submitting the site for Associates review.

flags.title: ThermoMaven: the maker's page and the listing make different claims about one thermometer
flags.detail: The maker's page (S21) states a 'bright, ultra-clear LCD' and a '100% waterproof design' with no IP code. The Amazon listing (S22) states an 'Auto-Rotate Bright LED Screen', 'IP67 Waterproof' and 'NIST&NSF Certified', and carries a 'newer model of this item' callout for B0GL7Z4KP4. The site publishes the maker's wording, records the listing's stronger claims as listing claims, and does not upgrade 'waterproof design' to IP67 on a retailer's word.
flags.impact: Display type and water resistance are published with both versions visible instead of one being chosen silently.
flags.manual_step: Ask ThermoMaven whether the F1 Ace is IP67 and NSF certified as the listing states, and whether B0GL7Z4KP4 supersedes B0DHZTCNR5.

flags.title: Analytics endpoint is not deployed; analytics is inactive on the live site
flags.detail: GitHub Pages serves static files and cannot run the collector. The client code is present but sends nothing until an endpoint is configured in data/config.json. The collector (tools/collector.mjs) is self-hostable. No clicks or conversions are being recorded on the live site yet.
flags.manual_step: Choose a hosting option for the collector (suggestion S-03). Then set analyticsEndpoint in data/config.json and rebuild.

flags.title: Disclosure placement needs manual review on real devices
flags.detail: The disclosure strip is placed under the masthead on every page and repeated in the footer, using the statement required by Operating Agreement §5 (S01). FTC guidance asks that disclosures be placed where they are hard to miss and near the link (S07, S08). Automated checks confirm presence, not visibility on a phone.
flags.manual_step: Open the live site on a phone-sized screen and confirm the strip is visible without scrolling on the home page and on a guide page.

flags.title: Tracking ID format matches Associates convention; ownership not confirmed
flags.detail: shopnow047c-20 ends in -20, the form Associates help describes for the US program (S03). The sandbox cannot confirm that the ID belongs to the signed-in account.
flags.manual_step: In Associates Central, confirm that shopnow047c-20 is listed as a tracking ID on the account.

flags.title: No Amazon-owned ASIN definition was retrieved
flags.detail: Searches returned third-party explanations of ASINs. No Amazon-owned definitional page was located, so the 10-character rule is supported only by the observed amazon.com identifiers (S04) and secondary sources.
flags.manual_step: Locate an Amazon Seller Central or Associates help page that defines the ASIN and add it to the source register.

flags.title: Google Search Console is not connected
flags.detail: The sitemap and feed are generated, and robots.txt references the sitemap. Search Console ownership verification needs a signed-in Google account, which the sandbox does not have. No verification token has been created or added.
flags.manual_step: Add the site as a URL-prefix property in Search Console, verify it, and submit sitemap.xml.

flags.title: Author is a team byline, not a named person
flags.detail: No named author, credential or biography is supplied, so the site uses 'Affil3 editorial team'. Inventing a person would be a fabrication.
flags.manual_step: Decide on a named author and bio (suggestion S-06).

flags.title: No product imagery is used
flags.detail: Amazon product images are Program Content. The IP License limits use of Program Content to the Associates purposes (S02), so the site uses typography and no product photography. Imagery is a decision (suggestion S-05).
flags.manual_step: Decide the imagery approach (suggestion S-05).

flags.title: Prices, ratings and availability are not recorded
flags.detail: Prices and ratings were visible only in carousel items on the fetched pages, not as confirmed values for the observed product. They change over time. Nothing is recorded or displayed, so no unverified number appears on the site.
flags.manual_step: If prices are wanted, decide the approach (suggestion S-10) and capture them only with a dated observation from an authorized source.

flags.title: Parallel sessions claim the same task on separate branches
flags.detail: Five other arena/*-affil3 branches on origin each claim the same overall task and each has its own COORDINATION.md. They were read (not modified) to check for overlap. Merging them to main will conflict. This branch builds at the repository root and uses its own file names to limit collisions, but a single integration branch should be chosen by the user. The other session's site (PR #1) is preserved unchanged at legacy/arena-83a43a96/ and is not linked from this site.
flags.manual_step: Choose which branch becomes the integration branch, or close the others.

flags.title: Repository review: the starting repo had only a one-line README
flags.detail: The repository had one commit with a README.md containing '# Affil3'. No code, data, configuration or history beyond that was present, so there were no existing irregularities to review.
flags.manual_step: None.

flags.title: Branch naming request differs from the session rule
flags.detail: The brief asks for session-<id>/<task> branches. This session may only work on its assigned branch, arena/6249757a-affil3, so all work is committed there and the PR is opened from it.
flags.manual_step: None unless you want a different naming policy.

flags.title: GitHub Pages source could not be changed from this session
flags.detail: The sandbox token returned HTTP 403 ('Resource not accessible by integration') when switching Pages to main /docs. Pages therefore serves main at the repository root. To publish one site without changing settings, this site is generated at the repository root and the earlier root-level site (PR #1) was moved, unchanged, to legacy/arena-83a43a96/. Nothing was deleted. To serve a different folder, change Settings > Pages.
flags.manual_step: Optional: if you prefer the site under /docs, change Settings > Pages > Source to main /docs, then remove the root copies.

flags.title: Thermometer guide omitted the FSIS ground-meat row; corrected
flags.detail: The guide 'Is your meat thermometer telling you the right number?' listed beef, poultry and ham minimums but omitted the FSIS row 'Ground Meats: 160 degrees F'. Corrected on 2026-11-20 by adding 'Ground meats: 160 °F.' to the list, matching the FSIS chart. The other listed values (beef/pork/veal/lamb 145 °F with a 3-minute rest; ground poultry 165 °F; all poultry 165 °F; uncooked ham 145 °F with a 3-minute rest) were checked against the same chart and match. Probe-placement statements for whole poultry were checked against the FSIS Food Thermometers factsheet and match.

flags.title: Two product destinations were transposed in the root-site register (corrected)
flags.detail: data/products.json recorded B08DKYBTPH (Chefman 8 Qt air fryer) as the destination of B0c8moW59, and recorded B00hJ57DV as unresolved. Both were wrong. Re-fetched twice on 2026-11-20: B00hJ57DV resolves to B08DKYBTPH and B0c8moW59 resolves to B0DHZTCNR5 (ThermoMaven 1 Sec meat thermometer). The two destinations had been swapped between the two rows. The editorial register at data/register/products.json reached the same destinations by a separate session, which corroborates the correction. Both records now carry a "reverification" block preserving the earlier value, so the fix is auditable rather than silent.
flags.impact: Before the fix the root site attributed a meat thermometer to the wrong submitted link, listed an air fryer as unresolved, and had two category assignments wrong.
flags.resolution: P03 and P04 corrected in data/products.json; previous values retained in each record's reverification block. FLG-004 marked resolved. Category pages, shop table and guide cross-links regenerated. Check both by hand: https://link.amazon/B00hJ57DV should land on https://www.amazon.com/dp/B08DKYBTPH, and https://link.amazon/B0c8moW59 should land on https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0DHZTCNR5
flags.detected_by: session arena/166bf329-affil3, cross-checking independently resolved short links against the stored register

flags.title: CHEF iQ battery life: the manufacturer's own pages disagree
flags.detail: The CHEF iQ Sense product page states '70+ Hours of Battery'. The CHEF iQ Sense FAQ on the same domain states that Gen 3 probes hold a charge for 'up to 60 hours'. Both are official CHEF iQ pages, so this site publishes no battery figure at all rather than choosing the friendlier one. The ambient temperature range, sensor count and probe dimensions on the product page are not in dispute and are published.
flags.impact: One marketing figure is unusable. No other specification is affected.
flags.manual_step: Ask CHEF iQ support which figure applies to the Gen 3 unit sold under B0DZFD6R9Z, or leave the battery field blank.

flags.title: Emeril Lagasse 26 QT: preset and accessory counts differ across official pages
flags.detail: The Emeril Everyday product page shows '25 Cooking Pre-sets' in its specification strip and '24 one-touch cooking presets' in its own description, and an image on the same page reads '11-in-1'. The Amazon listing title says '24 One-Touch Preset Options' and 'Six Cooking Accessories Included', while the manufacturer description mentions seven. Because the official sources conflict, this site publishes no preset count and no accessory count.
flags.impact: Two secondary specifications are withheld. Capacity, dimensions and form factor are unaffected.
flags.manual_step: Check the printed quick-start guide in the box, which is the only source that decides it for a shipped unit.

flags.title: ThermoMaven: the manufacturer page exists, and it is narrower than the listing
flags.detail: An earlier pass concluded that no manufacturer page existed for the ThermoMaven unit and withheld every specification and the buy link. That conclusion was wrong: thermomaven.com/products/f1-ace is the maker's own page and was fetched in full on 2026-11-20 (S21). It states the 1-second thermocouple read, NIST-certified +/-0.5 F accuracy, a 'bright, ultra-clear LCD' display, motion-sensing wake/sleep, a '100% waterproof design' with no IP code, a built-in magnet, and a lifetime warranty on registration within 30 days. It states no model number, no maximum ambient or leave-in temperature, and no IP rating. Those specifications are now published where the maker states them and left blank where it does not. Where the Amazon listing (S22) goes further - 'Auto-Rotate Bright LED Screen', 'IP67 Waterproof', 'NIST&NSF Certified', a 1x AAA battery - the claims are recorded as listing claims, and the listing's 'newer model of this item' callout (B0GL7Z4KP4) is published so a reader knows a successor SKU exists.
flags.impact: One of five products was published with no specifications and no buy link on the strength of a search that missed the maker's page. Both are now published, and four cross-channel differences are visible instead of hidden.
flags.manual_step: Confirm with ThermoMaven whether the F1 Ace is IP67 and NSF certified as the listing claims, and whether B0GL7Z4KP4 supersedes B0DHZTCNR5.

flags.title: The 8 Qt air fryer conflict was measured against the wrong model page (corrected)
flags.detail: The Amazon listing for B08DKYBTPH states 1000 W/120 V, model RJ38-SQSS-8T, 200-400 F, 12.75 x 13.5 x 10 in and a stainless-steel finish. An earlier pass compared that listing against Chefman's page for RJ38-8T-BLACK (1700 W, 450 F Hi-Fry, matte black) and concluded that two different machines shared one listing. That was the wrong comparison: Chefman also publishes a page for RJ38-SQSS-8T itself (S19), which states 8 qt / 7.57 L, 200-400 F, 1700 W/120 V, 15.4 x 12.6 x 13.5 in and 12.8 lb. Against the correct page the two agree on capacity, model number and the 200-400 F range, and disagree on wattage (1000 W vs 1700 W) and case size (12.75 x 13.5 x 10 vs 15.4 x 12.6 x 13.5). The manufacturer figures are published for this model and both differences are named.
flags.impact: Wattage and case size stay contested; capacity, model number and the temperature range are published because the correct maker page was located.
flags.manual_step: Confirm the wattage and case dimensions for RJ38-SQSS-8T with Chefman support in writing, and confirm whether the listing ships this model or a successor.

flags.title: One Amazon listing states two different temperature ceilings
flags.detail: The Amazon listing for B08DKYBTPH advertises a '450 F Hi-Fry option' in its title while its own 'About this item' bullet and the maker's page for the same model number (S19) both state a 200-400 F range. A short Hi-Fry burst above the normal ceiling is plausible and common, but neither page explains how it works, so the 450 F figure is not adopted. The site publishes the 400 F range that both the maker and the listing's own bullet state, and records the title's claim here.
flags.impact: The temperature ceiling is published with the title claim named rather than silently dropped.
flags.manual_step: The user guide linked from the listing should settle whether Hi-Fry is a separate short-lived mode. Read it and record the page reference.

flags.title: Amazon links were published without the tracking tag, including the citations
flags.detail: Program Policies 2(b) requires the Associates ID as a URL parameter on every link placed on the site, not only on buy buttons. The site linked the observed Amazon page in the source column of the shop table and on product pages, and published the supplied link.amazon short links as clickable links, none of which carried tag=shopnow047c-20.
flags.manual_step: None. The build now enforces the rule on every page: any link to an Amazon retail host gets the tag and rel=sponsored, and a link.amazon short link is rendered as text because it cannot carry the tag.
flags.resolution: Build-level link policy added and asserted by the gate on every page (retail Amazon link must carry the tag; no short link may be published as a link). Check count rose from 1,610 to 2,805.

flags.title: Every thermometer page referenced an image that was never committed
flags.detail: Fourteen references pointed at /assets/img/hero-thermometer.jpg, which did not exist in the repository. The category page, both thermometer product pages, the guides index and the thermometer guide would have shown a broken image on the live site.
flags.manual_step: None. The image was created in the same photographic style as the other hero images and committed; the gate now checks that every referenced image exists, is served locally, and has alt text.
flags.resolution: Image added on 2026-11-20. The image check was added to the gate, so a missing image fails the build from now on.

flags.title: Independent fetch by session arena63534e5d corroborated the corrected P03/P04 mapping
flags.detail: During the publication polish pass, an unauthenticated fetch observed B00hJ57DV resolving to B08DKYBTPH (Chefman 8 Qt) and B0c8moW59 landing on an intermittent checkpoint. Both observations agree with the corrected register: P03's mapping to B08DKYBTPH was confirmed independently, and P04's checkpoint matches the intermittent behavior recorded in FLG-004/FLG-022 rather than a dead link. Draft numbers this flag previously held on the session branch (FLG-021, FLG-023, FLG-028) all belong to other sessions' published findings, so it is recorded here as FLG-028's successor number FLG-030.

flags.title: A second publication at /docs/ publishes Amazon prices and star ratings
flags.detail: This domain serves two separate sites. The root site is generated from data/*.json and shows no prices or ratings. A second, older publication at /docs/ is still live and puts a current Amazon price (for example a four-figure-cent price for the 6 Qt basket) next to star ratings and review counts on its front page and product pages. Amazon's Program Policies allow a site to display price and availability only if Amazon serves that data or it comes through the Creators or PA API. That page does neither, and the figures it shows are now stale, which also makes them a misleading claim. The /docs/ build is git-ignored, is not produced by any current pipeline, and is a leftover from an earlier session's generator.
flags.impact: A live page on the same domain as the compliant site carries a price-display violation and stale ratings. This is the highest-risk item on the domain.
flags.manual_step: Retired in this session: the directory was removed and a redirect page now stands in its place, so the URL keeps working while showing no prices. If the earlier edition is ever wanted back, it must be regenerated without price or rating fields first.

flags.title: Every resolved destination carries a fallback marker, so “resolved” reads stronger than it is
flags.detail: All four submitted links that reached a product page landed on a URL carrying the query parameter plpRedirect=mhFallback, and in every case the ASIN of the page reached differs from the token in the submitted link. A marker of that shape means the router did not find the requested item and served something else. The product register records identity_status resolved on the basis of listing-title and manufacturer-page agreement, which identifies the page reached but cannot show it is the page intended. Observed 2026-11-20 by session arena-43565031-affil3; verbatim sources in evidence/43565031/.
flags.manual_step: Open each submitted link in a signed-in browser, read the ASIN from the address bar, and compare it with the ASIN the owner meant. A mismatch is an input error to fix at source, not a mapping to publish.

flags.title: Two sessions recorded different outcomes for the same tokens
flags.detail: One record in this repo has B00hJ57DV as the link that hit an Amazon “Continue shopping” checkpoint. On an independent retrieval the same day, B00hJ57DV resolved to a product page (ASIN B08DKYBTPH) and it was B0c8moW59 that hit the checkpoint. Both records are kept and neither is overwritten. Read together they show the outcome depends on session, timing or routing rather than on the token, and that any re-verification job must append attempts rather than replace a row. Observed 2026-11-20 by session arena-43565031-affil3; verbatim sources in evidence/43565031/.
flags.manual_step: Re-run each of the five links twice from a private window a few minutes apart and record the ASIN each time before treating any mapping as stable.

flags.title: Program Policies forbid tying a sub-tag or program identifier to a specific end user
flags.detail: Participation Requirements 2(b): “Under no circumstances may you associate any sub-tag, other ID or reporting provided in connection with the Associates Program with a specific end user of your Site (e.g., you may not dynamically assign sub-tags to users as they arrive on your Site for purposes of monitoring such users' behavior).” The site ships a client event emitter and a self-hosted collector under tools/analytics-endpoint. The event fields as specified (path, referrer_host, product_id, destination_host) carry no visitor identifier, which is consistent with the rule; the risk is the future join, which looks like ordinary analytics. Observed 2026-11-20 by session arena-43565031-affil3; verbatim sources in evidence/43565031/.
flags.manual_step: Before the collector is enabled, assert in the build that no sub-tag value is derived from anything persisted in the browser, and keep per-page sub-tags static strings.

flags.title: The three-qualifying-sales-in-180-days condition is not in the policy text retrieved here
flags.detail: Repeated widely across third-party affiliate guides as the condition for remaining in the programme and for API access. It does not appear in the Operating Agreement (updated 2025-10-15) or the Program Policies (updated 2026-04-14) as fetched on 2026-11-20. Nothing on this site relies on it; flagged so no launch date or account-risk assumption is built on it either. Observed 2026-11-20 by session arena-43565031-affil3; verbatim sources in evidence/43565031/.
flags.manual_step: Read the enrolment notices and the Participation Requirements in a logged-in Associates session, where the current conditions render in full, and settle this row either way.

flags.title: Attribution is a 24-hour session plus an 89-day cart path, not 90 days
flags.detail: Commission Income Statement 1(b) ends the Session at the first of 24 hours elapsed, an order placed, or a click through another associate's link; 1(c)(i) allows the cart route to complete “no later than 89 days after their initial click-through”. Guides online say 90 days. Any report, ledger note or article mentioning an attribution window must use 24 hours and 89 days. Observed 2026-11-20 by session arena-43565031-affil3; verbatim sources in evidence/43565031/.
flags.manual_step: Set the ledger's window definition from the policy line when the first row is written, not from a guide.

flags.title: CI asserts a directory the build does not write, so stale generated output merges green
flags.detail: .github/workflows/verify.yml runs tools/build.py and then asserts `git diff --quiet -- docs`. tools/build.py writes the site into editorial/ (its print statement still says docs/). Rebuilding in this branch produced a 5-line difference in editorial/assets/site.css against the committed copy, which that assertion cannot see. Root pages are regenerated by a second, separate generator (tools/build.mjs), which CI does not run at all. Observed 2026-11-20 by session arena-43565031-affil3; verbatim sources in evidence/43565031/.
flags.manual_step: Assert `git diff --quiet -- editorial` after build.py, and add a build.mjs step with its own diff assertion, so neither publisher can ship output that has drifted from its data.
flags.resolution: Current .github/workflows/verify.yml runs `npm run check` (both generators, both gates) and then fails if `git status --porcelain` is non-empty, which asserts the whole tree rather than any single directory. The gap described here no longer exists.

flags.title: The Operating Agreement section cited for the Associates statement was checked against the text
flags.detail: data/sources.json attributes the required statement and the no-embellishment rule to Section 5 of the Agreement, which is worth double-checking because the same wording also appears in help-centre articles. Observed 2026-11-20 by session arena-43565031-affil3; verbatim sources in evidence/43565031/.
flags.manual_step: None. Recorded so a reviewer does not re-open it.
flags.resolution: Confirmed correct on 2026-11-20 against the Agreement updated 2025-10-15. Section 5 is headed Identifying Yourself as an Associate and reads: “You must clearly and prominently state the following, or any substantially similar statement previously allowed under this Agreement, on your Site or any other location where Amazon may authorize your display or other use of Program Content: ‘As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.’” Section 6 adds that any violation of Section 5 will be deemed a material breach, and Section 4 states Amazon makes no representation about expected traffic or commission income — the basis for publishing no revenue forecast.

flags.title: A committed docs/ edition was being served without the FTC example disclosure and with hardcoded prices
flags.detail: tools/disclosure-check.mjs reported 37 problems, all of them under docs/: pages of a committed spare edition that display current price figures for several products and omit the disclosure sentence this repository's own gate enforces. Program Policies 2(b) allow a site to show prices only when Amazon serves them or a licensed Creators/PA API feed supplies them, so a committed copy of the site under docs/ is not a harmless spare: while Pages publishes / it is a second published edition, reachable at /Affil3/docs/, breaching the price rule on every one of those pages. The repo's .gitignore already says this tree must never be committed — “Never commit a regenerated legacy tree at the repository root”, with /docs/ listed — but the rule arrived after the files were tracked, so it had no effect. Note that even naming the offending figures on this page would breach the same rule, which is why they are described here rather than quoted; the gate caught exactly that in this flag's first draft. Observed 2026-11-20 by session arena-43565031-affil3.
flags.manual_step: The owner of whatever writes docs/ should point its output outside the served root, or rebuild it from the same disclosure partial as the root site. Untracking stops the live exposure; it does not settle which edition is canonical.
flags.resolution: Superseded by FLG-031: docs/ was deleted from the tree and gitignored; a single tracked noindex redirect page now stands at /docs/ so old links still resolve. The price and disclosure exposure ended when the edition was removed.

flags.title: A resolved merge conflict was committed into a frozen legacy page
flags.detail: legacy/categories/unresolved/index.html contains a literal <<<<<<< / ======= / >>>>>>> conflict marker on main, so a conflict was committed rather than resolved. It is inside the archive rather than the live site, which is why check_site.py does not see it, and it renders as visible junk text on a served page. Not this session's edit and not repaired here, because legacy/ belongs to whoever froze it. Observed 2026-11-20 by session arena-43565031-affil3.
flags.manual_step: Owner of that archive: resolve the marker in place, or re-freeze the edition from its source commit. A one-line repair, but it changes another session's frozen record, so it is logged rather than done.
flags.resolution: Fixed during integration session arena-78c96140: the conflict markers in legacy/categories/unresolved/index.html were resolved to the archived edition's own content, and the page renders without conflict junk again.
